svg.aria-label: Diagram: which Google Cloud VPC resources are global and which are regional, why the network itself has no address range so subnet CIDRs need only be unique within it, the asymmetric subnet range rules including reserved addresses and expansion, and two operational behaviours that mislead operators
svg.title: VPC networks: a global, address-less container whose subnets carry the ranges
svg.text: The network is global and has no address range. The subnets carry the addresses.
Which means there is no network-level CIDR to plan, and subnet ranges need not relate to each other.
What is global, and what is regional
GLOBAL: the VPC network, its routes, and its firewall rules. Not tied to any region or zone.
REGIONAL: subnets, and the IP ranges. A subnet is not the same thing as a VPC network.
One project can contain multiple VPC networks; one network can mix IPv4, dual-stack and
IPv6-only subnets in any combination.
And the network itself has no address range at all
There is no network-level CIDR to plan. The subnets carry the addresses, and they need only
be unique within the network: each primary or secondary range must be a unique valid CIDR.
The docs example makes the point: subnet1 is 10.240.0.0/24 in us-west1 and subnet2 is
192.168.1.0/24 in us-east1 — unrelated ranges, in one network, and that is fine.
The range rules, which are asymmetric in one place
Size: /29 at the smallest (eight addresses), /4 at the largest, with /8 the recommended cap.
A primary range can be EXPANDED but never replaced or shrunk. Plan for growth, not tidiness.
A secondary range can be removed or replaced, but only while no instances are using it.
Reserved: FOUR addresses in every primary range. ZERO in a secondary range.
Two things that will mislead an operator
Firewall rules are global resources but enforced ON THE VM, so traffic can only be controlled
and logged as it leaves or arrives at a VM. No choke point between subnets to inspect.
And the subnet gateway does not respond to ICMP or decrement TTL. It will not answer ping and
will not appear in traceroute, so a gateway-ping health check fails on a healthy network.
No broadcast, no multicast within the network. Legacy networks can no longer be created.
Overlay networks are outside what Cloud Customer Care will help configure or troubleshoot.
Thirty posts of IAM asked who may act. The network asks where packets may go, and the first
surprise is that the thing called a network is an address-less global container.
